name: project-setup
description: 'Sets up Toolkit V2 in a new project, or checks, updates, and repairs an existing setup, including Notion and Hindsight. Use when the owner says "set up Toolkit V2", "set up this project", "check the setup", or "update the toolkit", or starts working on a new computer.'

# Project setup

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Sets up Toolkit V2, never the older claude-toolkit (its `project-init` skill).

## Steps

1. **Check the computer and the project.** `toolkit` not found, or doctor
   reports a computer problem: `references/repair-and-update.md`, "Reaching
   the `toolkit` command".
   `toolkit doctor`
2. **Pick the path.** `.toolkit.json` present: step 8. A new computer:
   `references/new-computer.md`. Switching memory or tracker:
   `references/switching.md`. Otherwise a new project: put the checklist
   below in the plan tool (Claude Code: the task list; Codex: `update_plan`).
3. **Interview**, one question per message, each with a recommendation:
   name, tracker, memory, Salesforce, `SOUL.md`, backup folder. Look before
   asking. `references/interview.md`. Notion or Hindsight chosen: do the
   "Before init" part of its wiring file (step 5) now.
4. **Run init** with the answers, then record what it has no flag for.
   Inside Codex, say first that Codex will ask to run it outside the sandbox.
   `references/running-init.md`.
   `toolkit init --name '<name>' --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner '<owner>' --backup-dir '<folder>' [--salesforce] [--decline SOUL.md]`
5. **Finish wiring each choice**: `references/wiring-notion.md`,
   `wiring-hindsight.md`, `wiring-github-jira.md`, `wiring-salesforce.md`.
6. **Fill the setup guides** with facts the owner confirmed; the one-sentence
   outcome is his to say. `references/finishing-setup.md`.
7. **Finish:** backups, doctor at 0 problems, owner steps in the reply and the
   focus, the first briefing, the report, the commit offer.
   `references/finishing-setup.md`.
8. **Repair or update:** one numbered table from doctor and the dry run; sync
   only after a yes; doctor again until 0 problems.
   `references/repair-and-update.md`.
   `toolkit sync --dry-run`

## New project checklist

```text
- [ ] Doctor run; computer problems fixed
- [ ] Looked before asking: Git repository, code, sfdx-project.json, older toolkit files
- [ ] Six answers: name (key, id prefix, owner), tracker, memory, Salesforce (org aliases), SOUL.md, backup folder
- [ ] Notion signed in and root page known, or Hindsight answering, before init
- [ ] toolkit init run; id prefix and Salesforce aliases recorded
- [ ] Each choice wired: Notion, Hindsight, GitHub or Jira, Salesforce API version
- [ ] Setup guides filled with confirmed facts; outcome asked for; prompts left listed
- [ ] First backup made, or the owner's no-backup choice reported
- [ ] Doctor at 0 problems (warnings only the other host can clear are the owner's)
- [ ] Owner steps in the reply; the ones doctor checks also in the current focus
- [ ] First briefing shown; the report given
- [ ] Commit offer made; commit only after a yes
```

## Gotchas

- Never change an answer the owner gave (hosts, tracker, memory, Salesforce,
  `SOUL.md`) to get past a failed command, and never set up in another folder
  and copy it over. Stop, say what failed, and say what he must approve or
  run.
- Setup is never a work item. Never create one for setup steps, and never add
  made-up owner questions to finish setup.
- The project's one-sentence outcome is the owner's answer, never a sentence
  worked out from the code, the tests, or the README.
- Init wires Notion and Hindsight itself, so it stops when `ntn` is not signed
  in, no Notion root page is known, or the Hindsight server does not answer.
  Get the backend ready before init.
- Inside Codex, init writes `.codex/` and `.agents/` first, which the sandbox
  refuses. It must run outside the sandbox, with the owner's approval.
- The machine-setup command changes `~/.codex/config.toml`. Get the owner's
  yes before its first run on a computer.
- Nothing is created outside this project without a yes: no GitHub
  repository, no Jira fields, no paid service, no Notion pages outside the "AI
  Agent Second Brain" page.
- Every step is safe to run again. Init writes `.toolkit.json` last, and a
  second run reuses what an earlier run made.
- Run each `toolkit` command alone, on its own line, in both hosts; one-line
  values in single quotes (`references/toolkit-commands.md`).

## Steps only the owner can do

Say each one plainly, with why, and wait. Never do them for him.

- **`ntn login`**: signs the Notion command-line tool into his Notion account.
  It opens a browser sign-in. Needed only for Notion, and only when
  `ntn whoami` fails.
- **Trust this project folder in Codex**: open Codex in the project folder
  and trust it when Codex asks. Until he does, Codex ignores the project's
  `.codex/config.toml`, which turns the other Toolkit V2 plugins on. Trust is
  tied to the folder path, so it is needed again after the folder moves.
- **Trust the hooks in Codex**: open Codex in the project, type `/hooks`, and
  trust the Toolkit V2 hooks. Codex skips plugin hooks until he does. Needed
  again after the hooks change or the project folder moves.
- **Approve Codex running init outside its sandbox**, when setup runs inside
  Codex, or run the command init printed in a terminal.
- **Start a new session** after setup, so the host loads the new settings, the
  Plain English style, and the Toolkit V2 skills.

## References

| File | Open it when |

| `references/interview.md` | Step 3: what to check before asking, and the six questions with their recommendations |
| `references/running-init.md` | Step 4: the init commands, what init writes and installs, a failed run, init inside Codex |

| `references/installing-hindsight.md` | Hindsight or Ollama is not installed on this Mac: the installs, the first start, the service |

| `references/repair-and-update.md` | Step 1 when `toolkit` is not found; step 8; updating the installed plugins |

# Finishing setup

Purpose: after init and wiring, fill the setup guides with confirmed facts,
set up backups, get doctor to 0 problems, record the owner's steps, and end
with the report and the commit offer.

## Contents

- Filling the setup guides
- SOUL.md
- Backups
- Doctor
- The owner's steps and the current focus
- The report
- The commit offer

## Filling the setup guides

The copied files start with a fill-in guide comment and hold
`<angle bracket>` prompts. Init fills the project name. The rest is filled only with
facts the owner confirmed, in this order:

1. **The project's outcome** in `AGENTS.md`. It is the owner's answer, never a
   sentence worked out from the code, the tests, or the README. Ask it as its
   own question, with a suggestion from the repository:

   > What should this project do for you, in one sentence? From the code I'd suggest: "Export invoices to the bank's CSV format every Friday."

   Until he answers, leave the outcome prompts in `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`,
   and `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, and list them in the report.
2. **The "Build, test, or deploy" row** under Commands in `AGENTS.md`. Ask,
   with a recommendation from what the repository shows (for example
   `npm test`).
3. **`PROJECT.md` and `README.md`.** Follow each file's guide. Ask only what
   the repository cannot answer.
4. **`PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`** (the outcome, phases, and work units) and
   **`requirements/SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md`** (accepted data model requirements):
   fill them only when the owner already knows the facts. On a new project
   they usually stay as they are and are listed as prompts left. The data
   model gets only accepted requirements, never a guess.
5. Delete each fill-in guide comment once its file is filled.

Never invent a fact to fill a prompt. Each prompt that is left goes in the
report, with the fact it needs.

## SOUL.md

- The owner said yes: fill it with his words and get his approval of the
  text.
- He said no before init: init had `--decline SOUL.md`, and the file was never
  installed.
- He turns it down after init: record the no, then delete the file, so sync
  never brings it back and doctor does not report it missing.

  ```text
  toolkit config set declined SOUL.md
  ```

  `toolkit config set declined none` undoes it.

## Backups

Init recorded the backup folder (`--backup-dir`). From now on
`toolkit work finish` and every handoff back up the parts that live only on
this computer, to `<backup folder>/<project key>-<YYYY-MM-DD>/`.

1. Make the first backup now, so a folder that cannot be reached (for
   example an external drive that is not connected) shows up during setup:

   ```text
   toolkit handoff-backup
   ```

2. It prints one line saying what it copied. A failure line goes in the
   report, with its fix.
3. The owner chose no folder (`none`), or init ran without one: say in the
   report that nothing is backed up, and that doctor will keep noting it.

What each backup holds, and restoring: `backup-and-restore.md` in this
folder.

## Doctor

Run doctor until it reports 0 problems:

```text
toolkit doctor
```

- Fix each problem with the fix doctor names, then run it again.
- A warning only the other host can clear (for example Codex hook trust, seen
  from Claude Code) is the owner's step. It does not block setup, and it does
  not make doctor fail when run from Claude Code.

## The owner's steps and the current focus

Setup is not a work item. Never create one for setup steps, and never add
made-up owner questions to finish setup.

| Owner step | In the reply | In the current focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ntn login` (Notion, when `ntn whoami` fails) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Trust this project folder in Codex (Codex asks when it opens the folder) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Trust the hooks in Codex (`/hooks`) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Approve Codex running init outside its sandbox | Yes | No |
| Start a new session | Yes | No |

A focus line for a step doctor checks is marked so a later session knows when
to drop it:

```markdown
- Trust this folder in Codex: open Codex here and trust the folder when it asks. Setup step; drop it when doctor stops reporting it.
- Trust the Toolkit V2 hooks in Codex: open Codex here, type /hooks, trust them. Setup step; drop it when doctor stops reporting it.
```

Save the focus. The format, the version check, and the fill-in guide on a new
project: `current-focus.md` in this folder. Read it with its version, change
it, and save the whole text with that version. Keep the `# Current focus`
title and set the "Last updated" line, for example
`Last updated: 2026-09-28, setup, agent`. Run only the save for this host.

```text
toolkit memory focus --json
toolkit memory focus --set-file - --expect <version>
toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
```

The first save is Claude Code, with the text in a quoted heredoc (the
command, the text, then a line holding only `EOF`). The second is Codex.

Then show the first briefing:

```text
toolkit brief
```

## The report

A short plain report, in this order:

1. What was set up, as a short list the owner can check: tracker, memory,
   Salesforce or not, the files added.
2. What was skipped, and why.
3. What the owner must do himself, each with why.
4. Doctor's result: 0 problems, or each remaining problem with its fix.
5. The prompts left, each with the fact it needs.
6. The last line: the commit offer.

## The commit offer

The setup files are not committed yet, and the first merge of a work item
needs them committed. The reply's last line is:

> Setup files are not committed. Commit them now?

After a yes:

- Stage the files init wrote, each by name. Never `git add -A` or
  `git add .`.
- Read the staged list. No `.work-items/` or `.memory/` file may be in it.
- Commit with a plain message and no AI credit (for example
  `git commit -m 'Set up Toolkit V2'`).
- Codex: each Git command alone, with escalated permissions, or run by the
  owner in a terminal when Codex refuses it without asking.

The full rules: `git-rules.md` in this folder. After the commit, the reply's
last line is "Tell me the first thing you want built."

# Running `toolkit` commands

Purpose: how to run a `toolkit` command in Claude Code and in Codex, how to
pass text in one, and what each exit code means. Every skill that runs a
`toolkit` command follows this file.

## Contents

- Running toolkit commands
- Text in a command
- Exit codes
- Reporting a save
- Reading output and updating what you read
- Right and wrong examples

## Running toolkit commands

- Put each `toolkit` command on its own line and run it as a plain command,
  in both hosts. Do not join it to another command with `&&`, `;`, or a pipe,
  and do not wrap it in `$(...)`, a loop, or a script. This holds for read
  commands too: `toolkit work decisions && toolkit work show WI-001` is two
  commands, run one after the other.
- Why, in Codex: the project's command rule (`.codex/rules/toolkit.rules`)
  runs a `toolkit` command outside the sandbox only when it is the whole
  command. A `toolkit` command joined to anything else (`&&`, `;`, a pipe, a
  heredoc, `cd ... &&`) or run from a script (for example Python's
  `subprocess`) runs inside the Codex sandbox. The sandbox blocks Notion, the
  local Hindsight server, and the main checkout's `.work-items/` and
  `.memory/` from a worktree, so the command fails or reports the wrong
  cause.
- The one thing a Claude Code command may carry is its own text on standard
  input (`--set-file -` with a quoted heredoc; "Text in a command", below).
- Five commands ask the owner first, in both hosts, because they are hard or
  impossible to undo: `toolkit machine-setup`, `toolkit memory delete`,
  `toolkit memory import`, `toolkit import`, and
  `toolkit hindsight service install` or `start`. Get his yes in the reply
  before you run one. The host then asks him to confirm the command (Claude
  Code: a permission prompt; Codex: an approval). That prompt is expected, not
  an error.
- In Codex, run each of those five alone, with `sandbox_permissions` set to
  `require_escalated` and a one-line reason. The approval alone keeps the
  command inside the sandbox, where it fails: `toolkit memory delete` cannot
  reach Hindsight or Notion, `toolkit machine-setup` cannot write `~/.codex`
  or `~/.local/bin`, `toolkit hindsight service install` cannot write
  `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, and `toolkit import` from a worktree cannot write
  the main checkout.
- Write `--json` and `--host` after the command words
  (`toolkit memory delete <key> --owner-approved --json`). The toolkit refuses
  those five commands when a flag comes first, because the ask-first rules
  would not match them.
- Never change a work item or a memory record with a script or a shell write
  (Python, Node, `sed -i`, `cat >`, `tee`, `cp`). Use the `toolkit` command
  that owns it. The hooks refuse the shell write, so it only wastes a step.
- `toolkit help <command>` prints every option of one command.

## Text in a command

The shell changes text before the command sees it. Inside double quotes it
runs anything between backticks and anything in `$(...)` as a command, and
puts that command's output in the text. The command then saves the text with
those parts missing and still reports success. So:

- **One-line values** (`--note`, `--effect`, `--append-row`, `--title`,
  `--reason`, `--quote`, `--evidence`, `--description`, `--source`): put them
  in single quotes, in both hosts. Inside single quotes the shell changes
  nothing. Never use double quotes for text.
- **An apostrophe inside single quotes:**
  - Claude Code: write it as `'\''`, for example
    `--note 'Owner said: "it'\''s ready, ship it"'`.
  - Codex: write it as ’ (the curly apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the text.
    Never `'\''` in Codex: the command rule does not match that form, so the
    command runs inside the sandbox, and the tool call can drop the
    backslash, which leaves a quote that is never closed.
- **Section, design, focus, glossary, and memory text in Claude Code:** pass
  it on standard input with `--set-file -` (or `--body-file -` for a memory
  save) and a quoted heredoc. The quotes around `EOF` in `<<'EOF'` stop the
  shell from changing anything in the text, and no file is left anywhere.
  Claude Code refuses `rm` outside the project, so a temporary file there
  could never be deleted. Write the command, then the text, then a line
  holding only `EOF`:

  ```text
  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --set-file - <<'EOF'
  <the whole section text>
  EOF
  ```

- **The same text in Codex:** a heredoc runs the command inside the sandbox,
  so do not use one. Give short or medium text in single quotes
  (`--text '<text>'`; newlines inside the quotes are kept). For longer text:
  1. Make a new folder for this one save with `mktemp -d`. Its name is
     unique, so two sessions or two projects never share a file.
  2. Write the file in it with the file edit tool (`apply_patch`).
  3. Run the `toolkit` command alone, with the file's full path.
  4. Delete the file and the folder right after the command succeeds
     (`rm <file>`, then `rmdir <folder>`), before you ask the owner anything.

  Never write the file and run the `toolkit` command in one shell command.

  ```text
  toolkit work edit <id> --section 'Overview' --text '<text>'
  toolkit work design <id> --text '<text>' --status proposed
  toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
  ```

- Never use a fixed file name such as `/tmp/wi001-requirements.md`. Every
  project starts at `WI-001`, so another session's save could land in this
  item.
- Never leave a draft file inside `.work-items/` or `.memory/`. A second
  `DESIGN.md`-shaped file there confuses the design lookup, and a stray note
  in `.memory/` is read as a memory.

## Exit codes

`toolkit help work` prints them as: "0 ok, 1 error, 2 validation failure or a
refused gate, 3 not supported for this tracker, 4 not a toolkit project."
`toolkit help memory` uses the same numbers: "1 error or not found, 2 refused
(a rule or a stale --expect), 3 not supported by this backend".

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. | Read back what you wrote before you report it as saved ("Reporting a save", below). A "Note:" line in the output still needs action: report it to the owner, or do what it says. |
| `1` | Error, or the record was not found. | Read the message. It names the cause and usually the fix. Do not run the same command again unchanged. |
| `2` | Validation failure, a refused gate, or a stale `--expect`. | Fix what the message names and run the command again. A refused gate means an approval is missing: ask the owner for it. Never work around a refusal. |
| `3` | Not supported for this tracker or memory backend. | For a GitHub or Jira tracker, the message prints the path of the written instructions for that tracker. Follow them to make the same change on the issue. |
| `4` | Not a Toolkit V2 project. | Skip every work item and memory step and say so in one line. To set the project up, open the `project-setup` skill. |

`toolkit: command not found` means this computer cannot reach the command.
The `project-setup` skill fixes that.

## Reporting a save

- Save each settled answer before moving on, then read it back. A command
  that exits `0` is not proof by itself.
- A write failed: lead the reply with "Not saved". Name what was not saved
  and where it should go, and keep the text so it can be saved later.
- "Saved but not verified" in the output means the write happened and the
  read-back failed. The message names the first part that differs. Lead the
  reply with "Saved but not verified", say which part, and read the record
  back to judge it.

## Reading output and updating what you read

- Add `--json` when you need to read the output field by field, for example
  a record's `version`.
- `--expect <version>` tells the command which version of a record you read.
  The command refuses the save (exit `2`) when the record changed since then,
  so you never overwrite a newer edit. Read it again, merge, and save with the
  new version. `toolkit memory focus`, `toolkit memory glossary`, and
  `toolkit memory save` take it. `--expect absent` says it must not exist
  yet: a new record, or a project with no focus yet.

## Right and wrong examples

1. Two reads.
   - Wrong: `toolkit work list && toolkit work show WI-004`
   - Right: `toolkit work list`, then, as a second command,
     `toolkit work show WI-004`.
2. A history note that quotes the owner, with an apostrophe in his words.
   - Wrong: ``toolkit work history WI-004 --note "Owner said: it's ready, `ship it`"``
     (double quotes: the shell runs the words between the backticks as a
     command and saves its output in their place).
   - Right in Claude Code:
     `toolkit work history WI-004 --note 'Owner said: "it'\''s ready, ship it"'`
   - Right in Codex:
     `toolkit work history WI-004 --note 'Owner said: "it’s ready, ship it"'`
   - The prefix is `Owner said:`, which has no apostrophe to escape.
3. Section text in Codex.
   - Wrong: `cat > /tmp/overview.md <<'EOF' ... EOF && toolkit work edit WI-004 --section 'Overview' --set-file /tmp/overview.md`
     (one shell command, a heredoc, and a fixed file name).
   - Right: `toolkit work edit WI-004 --section 'Overview' --text '<text>'`
4. A change to a work item's header.
   - Wrong: `sed -i '' 's/^stage: .*/stage: 04-solution-design/' .work-items/WI-004/WORK-ITEM.md`
   - Right: `toolkit work set WI-004 --stage 04-solution-design --note '<why>'`
5. Toolkit commands from a script.
   - Wrong: `for id in WI-001 WI-002; do toolkit work show $id; done`
   - Right: `toolkit work show WI-001`, then `toolkit work show WI-002`, each
     as its own command.

# Running init, and what it installs

Purpose: the exact `toolkit init` commands, what init writes and in what
order, what to do when it stops, and which files each setup answer installs.

## Contents

- The init command
- What init does, in order
- A failed or stopped run
- Running init inside Codex
- What init installs
- How the answers shape the files

## The init command

Run one of these alone, with the owner's answers. One-line values go in
single quotes; write an apostrophe inside them as `'\''`.

```text
toolkit init --name '<name>' --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner '<owner>' --backup-dir '<folder>'
toolkit init --name '<name>' --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner '<owner>' --backup-dir '<folder>' --salesforce
```

- `--tracker`: `local`, `notion`, `github`, or `jira`.
- `--memory`: `builtin`, `hindsight`, or `notion`.
- `--backup-dir`: the folder from question 6, or `none`. Leave it out only
  with a Notion tracker and Notion memory.
- Add `--decline SOUL.md` after a no to question 5.
- `--hosts` defaults to both hosts (`claude-code,codex`). Leave it out unless
  the owner uses only one.

Example:

```text
toolkit init --name 'Acme CRM' --key acme-crm --tracker local --memory builtin --owner 'Mike Rihm' --backup-dir '~/Backups/toolkit' --decline SOUL.md
```

Then record what init has no flag for:

```text
toolkit config set tracker.idPrefix <prefix>
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.sandbox <alias>
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.production <alias>
```

The id prefix can change only before the first work item exists. The backup
folder changes later with `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or
`none`).

## What init does, in order

1. Works out the settings from the flags.
2. Plans every file. A setup marker error stops here, before any write.
3. Hindsight memory: checks that the local server answers. Nothing is written
   yet.
4. Wires the backends: builds the Notion pages and databases
   (`toolkit notion ensure-project`) and the Hindsight bank
   (`toolkit hindsight ensure-bank`) when chosen.
5. Writes the files: in Codex's own folders (`.codex/`, `.agents/`) first,
   then the rest.
6. Builds `.work-items/DASHBOARD.md` and `.memory/MEMORY.md`.
7. Writes `.toolkit.json`, last.

So a Notion or Hindsight project needs its backend ready before init runs:

Init stops, with nothing written, when the server does not answer.

1. Check the server:



     install the service.

   Ollama is not installed: `installing-hindsight.md` in this folder.

## What init does

`toolkit init` runs `toolkit hindsight ensure-bank` for you. It creates this
project's memory bank (one bank per project, named from the project key) and
writes the bank id into `.toolkit.json`. A bank with that id that belongs to
another project is never reused: the new bank gets `-2`, `-3`, and so on.

## After init, or to repair

```text
toolkit hindsight ensure-bank
```

Running it again changes only what is missing.

  Init then says the Codex sandbox blocked its request; the server may be
  fine. Show the owner the exact command init printed, and ask him to approve
  it or run it in a terminal (`running-init.md` in this folder).

  `toolkit memory export --to <folder>` (`backup-and-restore.md` in this

# The current focus

Purpose: the format of the current focus, when to change it, and the exact
read-change-save sequence, in every memory backend.

## Contents

- What the focus is for
- The format
- What goes in each section
- When to check it
- Read, change, save
- A new project's focus
- Examples
- Checklist for a focus save

## What the focus is for

The current focus is the first thing the next session reads: the session
briefing includes it. It says what is happening now and where the next
session starts. It never repeats the tracker: a work item's status, tasks,
and history stay in the work item.

| Backend | Where the focus lives |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in | `.memory/CURRENT_FOCUS.md` in the main checkout |
| Hindsight | The document `focus` in the project's bank |
| Notion | The "Current focus" page under the project's page |

The same commands read and save it in every backend. Never edit the file or
the page by hand.

## The format

The model's format: a `# Current focus` title line, a `Last updated:` line,
then exactly four `##` sections in this order, under 50 lines in total.

```markdown
# Current focus

Last updated: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <source>, <person or agent>

## Now

## Waiting on the owner

## Untracked to-dos

## Next session starts with
```

What the command enforces:

- It refuses a focus that lacks one of the four sections, has another
  section, or is over 50 lines (exit code 2, nothing saved).
- It adds the title line or the `Last updated:` line when either is missing,
  and sets an older date to today. It cannot know the source or who wrote
  it, so write the line yourself.

## What goes in each section

- **Last updated:** the date, the source (for example `handoff`,
  `work-finish`, `chat`), and who wrote it (a person, or `agent`). Change it
  on every save.
- **Now:** the current outcome or area, with work item ids and titles only,
  for example `- WI-012 CSV export`. Never a status or a stage: the tracker
  holds those.
- **Waiting on the owner:** a decision or action only the owner can take
  that has no work item: what it is, who needs it, and when to check again.
  Work items that wait on him are listed by `toolkit work decisions`, not
  here. A setup step (trust the hooks in Codex, sign in to Notion with
  `ntn login`) stays only while `toolkit doctor` still reports it.
- **Untracked to-dos:** things the owner asked for that have no work item.
  When one becomes a work item, replace the line with the item's id under
  Now.
- **Next session starts with:** one entry: where to resume, what to read,
  and the next action. It is replaced at each handoff, not added to.
- Write "None." in a section with nothing in it.
- Keep it under 50 lines by replacing stale lines, never by appending. Never
  drop an owner to-do that is still open only to meet the limit.

## When to check it

Check the focus before the reply ends when:

- a work item's stage changes, or its next step changes to something the
  focus does not say. Check two things:
  1. Now lists the item (id and title). Add it when it is missing; take it
     off when the item is Done or Cancelled.
  2. Next session starts with does not name a step that is done or no longer
     next. Replace that line with the item's real next step, in one line that
     points at the item, for example "Continue WI-012 from its Resume here:
     build P1."
- the owner asks for something with no work item (add it under Untracked
  to-dos), or a decision only he can make has no work item (Waiting on the
  owner).
- `toolkit doctor` no longer reports a setup step listed under Waiting on the
  owner (drop it).
- a session hands off (replace the one entry under Next session starts
  with).

Skip the save when nothing in the focus is wrong. Leave every line you are
not changing exactly as it is.

## Read, change, save

1. Read it with its version. The output has `text` and `version`:

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --json
   ```

2. Change only the lines that need it, in the whole text, and update the
   `Last updated:` line.
3. Save the whole text with the version you read.
   Claude Code: `<file>` is `-`, with the text on standard input after a
   quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`), then a line holding only `EOF`.

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --set-file <file> --expect <version>
   ```

   Codex: give the text in single quotes instead (newlines are kept), or
   use a file in a new `mktemp -d` folder and delete it after the save.
   Write an apostrophe as ’ (the curly apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the
   text. Never `'\''` in Codex: the project's command rule does not match
   that form, so the command runs inside the sandbox, and the tool call can
   drop the backslash.

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
   ```

4. Exit code 2 with "changed since it was read" means another session saved
   the focus after you read it. Read it again, make your change in the new
   text, and save with the new version. Never save without `--expect`: that
   would silently drop the other session's change.
5. No focus yet (`version` is null): save with `--expect absent`, in the full
   format above.
6. Read it back:

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus
   ```

## A new project's focus

A new project's focus still holds the model's setup text: a fill-in guide
comment under the title (`<!-- Fill-in guide: ... -->`) and an
`<angle-bracket>` prompt in every section. At the first save:

- remove the fill-in guide comment;
- replace each prompt with real content, or with "None." when there is none;
- never leave an angle-bracket prompt in a saved focus.

## Examples

A full focus:

```markdown
# Current focus

Last updated: 2026-09-26, handoff, agent

## Now

- WI-012 CSV export
- WI-015 Large exports (sub-item of WI-012)

## Waiting on the owner

- Pick a hosting provider before the first deploy (no work item yet); check again 2026-10-01.

## Untracked to-dos

- Email the client about the October demo.

## Next session starts with

- 2026-09-26 17:40 UTC | CSV export: continue WI-012 from its Resume here. Goal: exports finish under 10 seconds.
```

The handoff entry with a work item is a pointer only:
`<UTC date and time> | <topic>: continue <WI-id> from its Resume here. Goal: <one line>.`

With no work item, the entry is a short note: the goal or topic, where work
stopped, the first next action, limits on what may be done without the
owner, and open questions. Do not create a work item only to hold it.

## Checklist for a focus save

- [ ] Read with `--json`; you have the version.
- [ ] The `# Current focus` title and the `Last updated:` line (date,
      source, who) are there.
- [ ] Four sections, in order; "None." in each empty one.
- [ ] Work item ids and titles only; no status or stage.
- [ ] No angle-bracket prompt and no fill-in guide comment left.
- [ ] Under 50 lines; no open owner to-do dropped.
- [ ] Saved with `--expect`; read back.
